Repeat trick awards x0.5 of previous award; direction/degree change resets as new trick
Star multipliers 2x/3x/5x; only highest single star per jump; credited only on clean landing
6 individually landed ubers light TRICKY: infinite boost, permanent for run, two-in-one-jump counts two, resets between events

~3 mid-tier flip tricks fill meter empty to full; drains over time and on falls; repeats fill less

Camera smoothing frame-rate independent (split-step equivalence)
Position damping lambda 6-10 /s

No orbit in air: 900 deg air spin changes camera world yaw < 10 deg takeoff to landing
Air framing: follow distance +10-20% at apex; pitch relaxes toward horizontal keeping landing zone in frame
FOV kick relative to base, monotonic in speed, caps <= +20%, eases in faster than out
Trauma shake: magnitude = trauma^2, linear decay, clean-landing shake gone <= 0.5 s, rotational <= 5 deg at trauma 1
Boost FX ladder: higher tier strictly increases >= 2 speed cues; pickup grants top tier ~5 s

Trail refill multiplicative >= 0.999/frame at 60 fps for minutes-scale persistence (snowflow ~71%/min = 0.99990/frame), or documented arcade choice

Persistent visible board trail present whenever carving (2001 headline feature)
Sustained 60 fps on reference hardware
Saturated high-key palette; per-track colored gradient lighting allowed; shadows blue never black; big-trick celebratory FX

gates.statement: A STRAIGHT rail is survivable without a fight, and balance is not decoration. Two clauses: (a) a passive rider with NO input holds >90% of a straight rail and does not bail; (b) the stick MOVES balance — steer -1, 0 and +1 give measurably different balance, on opposite sides of neutral, so a module cannot satisfy (a) by pinning balance to zero.
gates.provenance: REWRITTEN 2026-08-27. The old gate demanded a passive rider BAIL off a straight rail in 0.8-6 s, which is the TONY HAWK balance meter (Pro Skater 2 onward). The reference bar is SSX, and references/research/02-turning-edge-friction.md sec 1.5 quotes StrategyWiki: 'To grind, just land on a rail, turn sideways to balance easier ... lock-on is automatic on contact, there is a light balance element handled by stance.' In SSX grinding is automatically balanced. The old model was also unplayable on a keyboard, which delivers +-1 or 0 rather than the proportional correction a divergent mode needs.

gates.statement: CURVES are the one balance failure the reference documents, and STRAIGHTS are not. Three clauses: (a) a straight rail holds a passive rider — the control; (b) a MODERATE bend (R=45 at 18 m/s) is ridden out with no input, because SSX rails are forgiving; (c) a FAST TIGHT bend (R=25 at 28 m/s) DROPS a passive rider and is rescued by steering. Measured: moderate max|balance| 0.25, tight 0.99.
gates.provenance: REWRITTEN 2026-08-27 with GR-05. The old gate graded 'a bend costs more stick than a straight' under a DIVERGENT balance mode that made straights cost stick too, so there was nothing to compare against. The documented failure is curvature-specific: references/research/02 sec 1.5 quotes a Tricky guide — 'I kept grinding but didn't turn. You eventually WILL FALL OFF for not turning.' Radius and entry speed are measured, not assumed: rail drag bleeds speed on a bend, so a slow rider on a tight bend is not loaded enough to fall. Fast-and-tight is what throws you.

gates.statement: The module never writes heading, and writes position only for the documented lock-on snap (max one snap per lock, <= captureRadius in magnitude)
gates.provenance: run-lane precedent: modules observe and constrain, they do not drive

gates.statement: No phantom locks: a rider 3 m off the rail line, or below minLockSpeed, never enters a grind
gates.provenance: anti-vacuity: a module that always locks would pass GR-01 trivially

gates.statement: Grind integration is dt-exact in the MODULE'S OWN state: one 100 ms step equals ten 10 ms steps in alongSpeed to 1e-6. (Position is deliberately NOT measured: GR-07 forbids the module from writing position, and physics integrates it with the project-wide Euler step, so exact position is not deliverable by any legal module.)
gates.provenance: project-wide integration rule (PC-02 precedent)

gates.statement: RETIRED 2026-08-26. Originally: 'a grind PRESERVES trick state - rail rotation survives the exit.' That is the OPPOSITE of the reference: in Tricky a rail spin RESETS when you leave the rail and open-air rotation needs a fresh input or a new prewind. The gate was unsatisfiable by any module using the constrained state and blocked three blind cycles. Its two real claims now live elsewhere: rail-spin accrual and reset are PC-19/PC-20/PC-21 (physics owns them), and the module-side coyote-branch damage is caught by GR-11, whose probe now includes an airborne window - verified: off-rail airTime pin 18 writes, on-rail pin 1 write, direct spinDeg write 431, honest baseline 0.
gates.provenance: REWRITTEN rails cycle 3. The old gate asserted rail spin must SURVIVE the exit and demanded spinPreservedFrac >= 0.9. The user supplied the reference: in Tricky a rail spin RESETS on exit and open-air rotation needs a fresh input or prewind. The old gate encoded the opposite of the bar, was unsatisfiable by any module using the constrained state, and blocked three cycles

gates.statement: The module never writes PHYSICS-OWNED TRICK STATE: spinDeg, flipDeg, airTime, charge, _popDone, spinCapped, flipCapped, prewound, landing. Probed with spin DRIVEN during the grind, so a module that only reaches for trick state when a spin input arrives is still caught
gates.provenance: blind critic, rails cycle 3: a candidate bought its entire scoreboard margin with two ps.spinDeg writes at source.mjs:363/427 - forbidden verbatim by CONTRACTS.md - because GR-07's watcher diffed only heading and position. Commenting out exactly those two lines dropped it to parity

gates.statement: A DESCENDING rail obeys the speed cap. Riding a 25 deg descending rail for 12 s must never exceed V_CAP (33 m/s) at any instant. Every other rail in this runner is flat, which hides gravity-along-tangent entirely
gates.provenance: blind critic, rails cycle 4: a candidate integrated alongSpeed with no clamp and reached 58.8 m/s on a 30 deg descending rail, leaking 63.95 m/s into the air on the pop. Every runner rail was flat so the whole GR sheet was blind to it. Adding a descending probe was recorded in BACKLOG at the previous rails stop and not actioned

gates.statement: A DESCENDING rail carries gravity along its tangent and beats the snow beside it. Riding a 25 deg descent must end FASTER than an identical rider on the snow alongside. Pairs with GR-12 so the cap gate cannot pass by nothing accelerating
gates.provenance: rails cycle 4 law repair. GR-12 initially passed on the baseline with railMax 18 == snowMax 18 and railEnd 5.85 vs snowEnd 15.75: the rail DECELERATED the rider because every test rail was flat and gravity-along-tangent was never implemented. Recorded at the previous rails stop, not actioned until now

gates.statement: HOW YOU LAND IS VISIBLE BUT NOT FATAL. A sloppy arrival (0.9 m off centre, -3 m/s lateral) must produce a measurably bigger balance excursion than a dead-centre landing — at least 0.15 — so the approach carries risk. It must NOT end the grind: under SSX a bad landing wobbles and settles.
gates.provenance: REWRITTEN 2026-08-27. The old gate required a sloppy arrival to BAIL sooner than a clean one, which only means anything when balance is a divergent mode — a settling one recovers by construction. Paired with the new GR-15 (the excursion must decay), this keeps the risk in the approach without importing the Tony Hawk death spiral.

gates.statement: A sloppy arrival SETTLES: the balance excursion it creates decays to under half its peak within 1.2 s and does not bail the rider. This is the SSX half of GR-14 — the landing matters, and then the rider recovers.
gates.provenance: Added 2026-08-27 alongside the GR-14 rewrite. Without it a module could satisfy GR-14 by making a bad landing catastrophic, which is exactly the Tony Hawk behaviour the reference bar rejects.

gates.statement: CONSTRAINED state charges: a rider held in the constrained state (rail/wallride/tow) accrues crouch charge at T_CHARGE exactly as on ground — 1.0 s of crouch reaches full charge
gates.provenance: BACKLOG option (a): a grind is supported, not free-falling; without this the rail-into-big-air link is unbuildable (measured 2.5 s crouch on a rail released at exactly J_MIN)

gates.statement: Releasing a charged jump from the constrained state pops at the FULL charged impulse (J_MAX band), not J_MIN, and leaves the constrained state as a true takeoff (rotation and air clock reset)
gates.provenance: same — this is the rail-into-big-air link

gates.statement: The constrained state does not FALL: no gravity is applied (vertical velocity unchanged, airTime held at 0). It does still MOVE — the constraint owner writes velocity and physics integrates it. The first version of this gate asserted position never changed at all, which froze the rider solid and made crouch-to-pop stop you dead mid-rail.
gates.provenance: same — physics runs the rider, the constraint owner runs the motion

gates.statement: THE MODULE DOES NOT CHANGE THE RUN IT TIMES: over an identical competent run, finish time and final score with the run module attached match a run with no module to within 0.5% — the corridor is a boundary, not a participant. A rider drifting back over the start line mid-run is normal play (a start GATE is not a wall), so the up-course correction line is bounds.zBackstop, not zStart
gates.provenance: measured residual on the promoted module: 261.5 s / 2284.5 pts with the module vs 266.4 s / 2099.1 without — 4.9 s and +8.8%, from one 20.5 m/s impulse when the rider flew 17.34 m up-course after a backwards jump

gates.statement: POST-LANDING RE-CONVERGENCE: after a 3 s air, camera-to-rider distance returns to within 15% of its steady-state value within 1.2 s of touchdown, and never exceeds 2.2x steady-state at any point in the landing transient — the rider must never shrink to a distant speck on the frame after a big air
gates.provenance: integration judge, round 4: 'the camera lags so far behind after the landing that the rider shrinks to a distant speck and speed sense/framing collapses — the one frame that stops reading as SSX'

gates.statement: A constrained rider ADVANCES: with velocity set by the constraint owner, physics integrates position — 1 s at 18 m/s moves ~18 m along the velocity direction
gates.provenance: blind critic, rails cycle 2: measured 0.00 m of advance over a 0.9 s charge — crouching to pop froze the rider

gates.statement: The board follows the rail: while constrained, heading converges to the velocity direction, so a rider leaving a curved rail is not crabbed (residual yaw vs velocity <= 5 deg after 0.5 s of a redirected constraint)
gates.provenance: blind critic, rails cycle 2: board frozen at pre-lock yaw exits a curved rail 27.1 deg crabbed after 39 deg of sweep; land() scores that sketchy, and >=90 deg is an unavoidable crash

gates.statement: RAIL SPIN EXISTS: a spin input held while CONSTRAINED rotates the rider on the rail (this is how you end up riding switch). 1.5 s of full stick at SPIN_STICK (300 deg/s) accrues >= 300 deg. Before this, spin input while constrained did nothing at all
gates.provenance: user-supplied reference, rails cycle 3: 'On rails, your spin inputs using the directional pad control your flat/rail spins and trick modifications for that specific grind'

gates.statement: RAIL SPIN RESETS ON EXIT: popping off a rail clears accumulated rotation. Open-air rotation requires a FRESH input or a new prewind - a rail spin never follows the rider into the air. This is the exact opposite of what GR-10 asserted for three cycles
gates.provenance: user-supplied reference, rails cycle 3: 'As soon as you pop off or disengage from the end of the rail, your rotation state resets. Any spin or flip you want to perform in open air requires a fresh input or a new pre-wind'

gates.statement: A rider who pops off MID RAIL SPIN does not leave crabbed: heading settles to the direction of travel as part of the reset, so land() cannot score an unavoidable crash on an exit the player had no way to square up. Measured at the worst case - jumpRelease on the same frame as full-stick spin
gates.provenance: derived from PC-20 + land(): without this a mid-spin pop exits up to 90 deg crabbed, which land() scores a crash

gates.statement: The V_CAP clamp applies in the CONSTRAINED state too, not just the ground core. A constraint owner writes velocity; physics still caps it. Probed by writing 80 m/s and -70 m/s directly and stepping once - the result must be <= V_CAP (33)
gates.provenance: blind critic, rails cycle 4: a candidate integrated alongSpeed with no clamp, reached 58.8 m/s on a 30 deg descending rail and leaked 63.95 m/s into the air. PC-06 only probed a boosted 45 deg slope inside groundCore, so no gate could see it. NOTE: airStep is deliberately NOT clamped - ballistic flight legitimately exceeds V_CAP in total speed during a long fall, and clamping it would corrupt the JA arcs. The cap belongs where velocity is SET, not where gravity integrates.

gates.statement: The BOOST ECONOMY runs in the constrained state: holding boost on a rail drains the meter, as it does on snow and in the air. 5 s of held boost must drain a real fraction of the meter (>= 0.3)
gates.provenance: blind critic, rails cycle 4: constrainedStep never called meterTick, so boost on a rail cost nothing - 0.971 meter left after 5 s of rail boost vs 0.375 on snow. Found by a candidate that correctly declined to patch physics from a rails module

gates.statement: PHYSICS OWNS THE RIDER'S MODE, and the CONSTRAINED state wins. Two claims: (1) PRECEDENCE - a rider who locks onto a rail from the SNOW (onGround still true) runs the constrained tick, not the ground tick, and the exported riderMode(state) returns 'constrained' | 'ground' | 'air' in exactly that order of precedence; (2) NO STALE FLAG - after every constrained tick st.onGround is false, because a constrained rider is held by something that is not the terrain. constrainedStep wrote neither, so the flag froze at its capture-frame value for the entire grind and every consumer outside physics read a leftover
gates.provenance: user defect 'the player literally falls right through the rail after a few feet', measured on the 9 real course rails in src/game/main.mjs advance() order (harness/rig-rail-fallthrough.mjs, 810 attempts). NOT geometric: 690 locks, 0 fall-through, worst sink 0.021 m against a 0.11 m tube. The frozen flag was the whole defect - index.html asked `if (st.onGround)` FIRST while step() asks `if (state.constrained)` FIRST, so a grind that captured with the flag false delivered the carve stick as `spin` and rails.mjs (which reads only inp.steer) got nothing: 118 bails in 119 such locks, median 12.40 m / 40.7 ft in, median 0.65 s, then a silent 0.56 m drop onto the snow under the rail line and she keeps riding. The 111 locks that captured with the flag true bailed 0 times and ran a median 58.20 m. Same intent through one shared router: 0 bails in 230 locks. The stale flag was also entry-dependent for the five other readers - rail0 ground entry flagged all 145 on-rail frames grounded, rail3 flagged all 152 airborne, same rider, same action

gates.statement: A rival drives the ACCEPTED physics through INPUTS ONLY. Replaying the rival's recorded input stream through a fresh createPhysics reproduces its trajectory to within 1e-6 m. Any direct write to pos/vel/heading makes this diverge immediately
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: The whole lane is worthless if rivals cheat physics. Mutant: have the module nudge ps.pos[0] by 0.01 once per second. All 40 tapes are replayed now.

gates.statement: Rival inputs stay inside the PLAYER'S input domain: steer/spin/flip in [-1,1], booleans actually boolean, uber in 1..6. No rival may pass a value the keyboard cannot produce
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: steer: 3.0 is the cheapest possible cheat and looks like nothing in a trace.

gates.statement: Every rival FINISHES. Across 8 seeds and 4 rivals, all 32 runs reach zFinish without getting stuck, reversing permanently, or leaving the course
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: A stuck rival is the single most visible AI failure. 32 runs, not 1 — a single lucky seed proves nothing.

gates.statement: Rivals stay in bounds: max lateral excursion beyond the course halfWidth is 0 m over every run in AI-03's matrix
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.

gates.statement: Rubber-banding is BOUNDED and one-directional: any catch-up assistance is off while the rival leads the player, and the assisted-to-unassisted finish-time ratio never exceeds 1.15. Measured by running the same seed with assistance forced off
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: Tricky rubber-bands and so should we. The gate is on the SIZE and the SIGN, not the existence. Mutant: apply catch-up while ahead. COVERAGE WIDENED BY THE 2026-08-27 AUDIT: the size clause read one live seed and two frozen-player races, and an audit module that rubber-banded at 1.31 on the other five seeds reported 1.08. Both clauses now sweep all 8 seeds. The honest baseline re-measures at 1.08 (it read 1.09 under the old sample, and 1.13 for the same module once every seed was in).

gates.statement: Catch-up is expressed through INPUTS or declared physics parameters, never as a raw grant: the module writes NO FIELD of a rival's or the player's physics state — not pos/vel/heading, and not the resources a cheat would spend from (charge, boostMeter, onGround, airTime, landing) — and a rival's sustained horizontal speed never exceeds what the accepted physics permits for its state (V_CAP, and V_BOOST while its own meter has charge)
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: WIDENED BY THE 2026-08-27 AUDIT. The probe diffed pos/vel/heading only, and an audit module that wrote self.boostMeter = 1 every frame and held the boost key scored 13/13 with an infinite meter. Those seven numbers are what a cheat SPENDS; the state also carries what it spends FROM. The diff is now over the whole state and the report names the field.

gates.statement: The easy tier is BEATABLE: a reference mid-skill player run (the harness' scripted racer) finishes ahead of every easy rival across 8 seeds
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.

gates.statement: The hard tier can WIN: the same reference mid-skill run finishes behind at least one hard rival across 8 seeds. A lane where the player always wins has no rivals in it
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: AI-07 and AI-08 must BOTH hold. Either alone is trivially satisfiable by making the AI uniformly slow or uniformly fast.

gates.statement: Tiers are ORDERED and separated: mean finish time easy > medium > hard across 8 seeds, with each gap at least 3% of the course time. Overlapping tiers are indistinguishable to a player
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.

gates.statement: Rivals RIDE, they do not rail a line: across a run each rival accumulates real airtime (>= 1.5 s total) off at least 3 CHARGED pops of its own (crouch charge >= 0.25 at the jumpRelease frame, so a twitch of the key is not a pop), and its lateral track VARIES - standard deviation of its offset from the centreline about its own mean >= 2 m, not merely distance from the centre. A rival pinned to a line reads as a moving cone wherever that line is
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: Written as PRESENCE of both behaviours so it cannot pass by absence — the failure this lane will actually produce is a perfect centreline follower. BOTH CLAUSES WERE TIGHTENED BY THE 2026-08-27 AUDIT: bare jumpRelease frames were satisfied by a module that twitched the key every 2 s with no crouch behind it (22 'pops', charge 0, ~0.22 m of hop), and RMS-from-centreline was satisfied by a module welded to a fixed 4.5 m offset (RMS 18.1 m, lateral standard deviation 1.35 m).

gates.statement: Rivals are DETERMINISTIC given a seed: two runs with the same seed produce byte-identical finish times and identical input streams, and INSTANCES ARE ISOLATED: writing into the config one instance hands out must not be visible to an instance constructed afterwards
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: Without this every other gate in this file is flaky and will be re-run until green. ISOLATION CLAUSE ADDED 2026-08-27. The HONEST BASELINE itself leaked: it handed out the module-level TIERS object by reference, so setting A.config.tiers.easy.stats.speed = 999 was visible in a FRESHLY constructed C, and this gate passed the whole time. The runner builds each rival's physics from cfg.tiers[tier].stats, so the leak changes every later race in the process. Probed structurally — deep-poison every number in the config a module returns, build a fresh instance, look for the poison — rather than by checking a list of field names, so a module that leaks some other table is caught too. Found by a cycle-3 critic.

gates.statement: Rivals do not interpenetrate the player or each other: minimum centre-to-centre separation over a full race is >= 0.6 m, and no rival remains within 1.0 m of the player for more than 2.0 s (no shepherding, no blocking-lock)
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.

gates.statement: PERFORMANCE: 5 rivals plus the player sustain 60 fps in the rig, the rivals' own update costs <= 1.5 ms/frame measured separately from render (including any work hidden in getters on the inputs it returns), and createRivals + init together fit inside ONE 60 Hz frame (16.7 ms) so the cost is not simply moved to the start gate
gates.provenance: references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json - rivals lane law draft, merged 2026-08-27; SSX Tricky rubber-band precedent per research 02. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition of every metric here.
gates._why: WIDENED BY THE 2026-08-27 AUDIT. Two audit modules passed at 0.001 ms/frame: one burned 166 ms inside init(), which the frame timer never sees, and one returned inputs whose GETTERS did the work, which sanitizeInput evaluated outside the timed window. The fps half of the statement is still NOT MEASURED here (browser-only) and the runner says so in a side field on every run.

gates.statement: Rivals ride LINES OF THEIR OWN, not one line at four throttles: with the throttle channel neutralised - every rival given identical stats, its boost/brake/uber discarded, its tuck pinned, and the start gate collapsed so nobody is handed a lateral head start - no two rivals' lateral offset profiles, each de-meaned to strip its lane, may sit closer than 5.0 m RMS over the course on any seed
gates.provenance: Added 2026-08-27 after rivals cycle 2 closed without shipping. harness/rival-runner.mjs is the operational definition; the metric is defined by laneProfile()/closestLinePair() there, and harness/rival-mutants.mjs holds the mutant that proves it.
gates._why: THE OTHER TWELVE AI GATES CANNOT SEE THIS. Measured, not argued: a module driving one shared line, phased on z so the path is byte-identical for all four riders, with constant 9 m lane offsets and tiers separated by throttle alone, scores 13/13 with hardFails 0 on the sheet as it stood. That module IS the gap the cycle-1 critic named, and it is now the AI-14 mutant. CALIBRATION on the real course, worst of 8 seeds: one line no lanes 0.00 | one line + 9 m lanes 2.33 | a crude four-line probe 3.05 | cycle-2 candidate B, which the critic independently judged to have an inert character axis, 3.52 | this baseline 9.47 | cycle-2 candidate A 9.56. The threshold sits above the mutant and above the inert candidate. THREE METRICS WERE BUILT AND DISPROVED FIRST, all by measurement against the train: raw pairwise lateral separation (dominated by lane pitch - it INVERTS, ranking the train above a real four-line field), a signed corner-bias index de-meaned and curvature-signed (train 2.09 against a 1.0 threshold, i.e. the gate passing its own mutant, because a rider parked off-centre takes a different-radius path and its tracking lag reads as bias), and that index with the lane regressed out across the field (train 1.78 vs an honest baseline 1.55 - four riders and two fitted parameters is mostly fit noise). DISCLOSED WEAKNESS: the throttle lock is detectable from inside a module, so a module could in principle ride distinct lines only while locked. Nothing here catches that. THRESHOLD: 5.0 sits between the two measured anchors on this course — the baseline-derived train mutant at 3.70 and the honest baseline at 11.21 — and is not derived from anything finer than that. It was first set at 4.0 and raised: the train failed it by only 7.5%, which is not a margin a mutant should be allowed. At 5.0 the mutant fails by 26% and the baseline passes by 124%. Cycle-2 candidate A, a real module with four distinct lines, measures 9.56, so the bar is clearable. CORRECTION 2026-08-27, found by a cycle-3 critic and not by me: every full-sheet number this gate reported before the fix was measured on UNLOCKED races. rival-runner's race cache keyed on seed/assist/player/roster/timeModule and omitted throttleLock, so the twelve gates ahead of AI-14 filled the cache with unlocked runs and lockedMatrix() got cache hits. The baseline read 11.21 poisoned and 9.47 clean. The mutant table was never affected — it runs --only AI-14, so lines() populates the cache first — which is also why calibration missed it: every calibration run took the correct path by accident. tests/suite.mjs now asserts a gate reads the same alone as in a full sheet, and that test is verified to fail on the old key.

rivalsLaneNotes._merged: 2026-08-27, merged from references/RIVALS_GATES.draft.json, which was deleted afterwards. Nothing in the draft is lost: its design notes, its mutant list and the two open questions it left to the user are all carried here.
designNotes: THE CENTRAL RULE: rivals ride the SAME physics as the player. They produce an INPUT each frame (the same {steer, tuck, boost, crouch, jumpRelease, spin, flip, grab, uber} shape the keyboard produces) and nothing else. A rival that writes velocity, position or heading directly is not a racer, it is a cutscene. This is the rivals-lane equivalent of the rails lane's GR-07/GR-11 and it is the gate most worth mutation-testing first.

SSX Tricky's AI is openly rubber-banded. The bar is not 'no catch-up' but 'catch-up you cannot see': bounded, off when the rival is ahead, and never expressed as raw speed the physics would not allow.
Every gate below must be reproducible from a seed. A flaky rival gate is worse than no gate — it trains everyone to re-run until green.
mutantsToWriteFirst: AI-01: nudge ps.pos[0] += 0.01 once per second — replay must diverge
AI-02: emit steer: 3.0 on one frame
AI-03: freeze one rival's input after 20 s — finishRate must drop
AI-05: apply catch-up while the rival is AHEAD
AI-06: grant +8 m/s directly when behind
AI-08: make the hard tier 20% slower — hardTierWins must fail
AI-09: set all three tiers to the same parameters
AI-10: pin the rival exactly to the centreline — must fail on BOTH clauses
AI-11: seed the rival RNG from Date.now()
resolvedByUser: COLLISION: rivals and the player PASS THROUGH each other. Decided 2026-08-27. The accepted physics has no rider-rider term and adding one changes the physics contract, so bumping/blocking gets its own gates if it is ever wanted. AI-12 was already written as a separation MEASUREMENT rather than a collision requirement, so it holds unchanged under this decision.

TRICKING: rivals RACE ONLY for now. They do not drive the trick system, do not score and do not build boost from tricks. Rivals that trick would mean rivals driving a second accepted module, which is a separate lane.
SAME PHYSICS: confirmed by the user. This was already AI-01 (inputs only, replay must reproduce the trajectory) and is not a new constraint.
openQuestionsResolved: Does the player collide with rivals, or pass through them? Collision is a physics-contract change (the accepted physics has no rider-rider term) and is a USER DECISION, not a builder's. AI-12 is written as a separation measurement so it holds either way.
Tricky's rivals also trick and build boost. Deferred: this draft races them only. Adding trick behaviour means rivals drive the trick system too, which is a second lane.
